chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
He recited: 'that they should put off their outer garments', he said: 'the jilbab and the khimar', when the woman has aged.

key_terms.الْجِلْبَابَ: The outer garment or cloak worn by women
key_terms.الْخِمَارَ: The headscarf or veil covering the head and neck
key_terms.مُسِنَّةً: An elderly woman, past the age of desire for marriage/adornment

ai.seo_question: What does 'put off their outer garments' mean in Surah An-Nur according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the phrase 'put off their outer garments' in Surah An-Nur refers to the jilbab and khimar, establishing a specific exemption for elderly women (musinnah) from strict hijab requirements in the presence of non-mahram men, provided they do not desire adornment. This interpretation highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding age and modesty, distinguishing between the general obligation of covering and the specific concessions for those past the age of marital desirability.
